next_experiments.hypothesis: H2 test: is the low-gravity upward flammability limit (ULOI*/MOC*) of candidate cabin materials below their 1-g NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 MOC at this atmosphere? Pair every low-g test with a 1-g test in the same atmosphere to compute the oxygen margin (Eq. 1).

checks.criterion: >= 3 independent partial-g campaigns, same variable and material class
>= 5 partial-g points reserved for external validation
Grouped (leave-one-campaign-out) conformal coverage within 0.85-0.95 and better than the physics baseline

assumptions: Gas properties (thermal diffusivity, expansion coefficient, flame-ambient temperature difference) are taken as independent of gravity level.
u_b is a characteristic velocity scale, not a flow field; real buoyant flows are non-uniform and depend on flame orientation.
Radiation and short-duration (transient) effects are neglected.
The 1-g anchor spans 20-35 cm/s across sources (NASA 2021: ~20 cm/s; Konno 2024: 35; Nakaya: 33), so every equivalence is anchor-dependent.

The g^(1/3) form applies when the length scale is the flame's thermal length (flame stabilization zone, opposed spread); for a fixed length scale (e.g. a small engulfed sample) NASA notes U ~ g^(1/2) instead (NTRS 20210020516 p. 20).
